title: Semantic compatibility matrix and tiered-region fallback orchestration for incremental experiments
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Design and implement a semantic compatibility matrix and orchestration layer that enables safe incremental experiments (canaries, A/B tests, shadowing) while providing deterministic fallback behavior across model variants, regions, and capacity tiers. This ticket covers: (1) a CI/runtime compatibility matrix for model variants, (2) routing policies that consider semantic compatibility and capacity tiers, (3) canary and A/B traffic ramp policies with automatic rollback triggers based on semantic/quality regressions, latency, and error metrics, and (4) cross-region tiered failover behavior that preserves privacy/SLO constraints.
acceptance_criteria: A compatibility matrix artifact is produced and checked into model onboarding (tokenizer, input schema, expected output schema, kv-cache format, required sequence length and memory footprint).
CI step runs compatibility tests that assert model variant passes input/response schema AND a small semantic-sanity eval before marking as deployable.
Runtime router uses the compatibility matrix to reject incompatible variants and transparently reroute to the most compatible fallback when needed.
Canary experiment flow implemented: 1% shadow+canary for 30m, automated ramp to 10% over 4h conditioned on metrics; configuration is exposed in the Console rollout UI.

Auto-rollback triggers implemented and tested in staging: sustained latency spike, >5% live error-rate increase, or semantic-drift metric (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity) degradation beyond threshold cause rollback and notification.

Tiered capacity fallback works across dedicated, hosted, and quantized variants: when dedicated pool is saturated, traffic reroutes to compatible quantized variant or lower-tier region per policy, with telemetry showing cost/latency delta.
Playbook and sample rollout YAML added to docs + one sample canary run recorded using synthetic and shadow traffic with results in Console.
tasks: Create compatibility matrix schema and JSON artifact for onboarding (tokenizer, vocab, max_seq, kv_cache_schema, decode_constraints)
Add CI job that loads new model artifact and runs schema + semantic-sanity checks (tiny eval set)
Extend routing engine to consult compatibility matrix and compute fallback chain at deploy-time and runtime
Implement canary/B test policy primitives: initial_shadow, traffic_split, ramp_schedule, health_checks
Implement auto-rollback controller with hysteresis and configurable thresholds
Add telemetry and Console UI hooks for canary windows, rollback decisions, and fallback events
Run cross-region failover simulation and produce runbook entries
Write integration tests that simulate tokenizer mismatch, kv-cache incompatibility, and capacity saturation to validate fallback behavior
decisions: Compatibility artifact will be a JSON 'compatibility matrix' checked in with model bundle and versioned via model catalog
Runtime will prefer transformation adapters (input transformation/tokenizer shim) when safe; if adapter not available, runtime will choose nearest compatible fallback variant
Auto-rollback will be proactive: rollback within 5 minutes after trigger sustained for 2 minutes or when 10% of requests are flagged by quality hooks
A/B statistical tests will use sequential testing (SPRT-like) for faster detection while controlling false positives
Shadow traffic will be recorded asynchronously and evaluated using offline quality metrics before being promoted to live traffic ramps
tradeoffs: Strict enforcement of compatibility matrix reduces risk of runtime failures but increases onboarding friction for new model variants
Adapters can reduce friction but add maintenance burden and potential latent correctness issues
Aggressive auto-rollback protects customers but may increase churn of deployments for noisy workloads; thresholds need tuning per customer SLA
Routing to quantized variants reduces cost but increases latency/quality uncertainty; must be visible in Console and auditable

notes: Implementation approach: treat compatibility matrix as contract between model-onboard and runtime. At deploy-time, compute candidate fallback chain ordered by semantic_compatibility_score + region/cost constraints. At runtime, route by policy: prefer same-region dedicated variant -> same-region hosted quantized -> cross-region dedicated -> cross-region hosted quantized. Each hop logs event with reason and pre/post latency+cost estimate. Canary flow: start with 1% canary as mirrored shadow requests + 0.1% live traffic, run deterministic checks, then ramp. Use offline replay for additional validation.
sample_yaml:
rollout:
  id: ENG-35421-sample
  initial_shadow: 1%
  live_split: 0.1%
  ramp_schedule:
    - after: 30m
      set_live_split: 1%
    - after: 4h
      set_live_split: 10%
  health_checks:
    latency_p90_ms: 1200
    error_rate_delta: 1.05
    semantic_similarity_drop: 0.92
  fallback_policy:
    prefer_same_region: true
    fallback_chain_limit: 3
  auto_rollback:
    sustained_window: 2m
    cooldown: 10m
    escalation_alert: SRE-oncall
developer_notes: Keep compatibility matrix small and opinionated initially: tokenizer_id, special_tokens_map, max_seq, kv_cache_version, decode_constraints, data_residency. We'll iterate to add model-behavior fingerprints next quarter. Consider a model-testing harness for fuzzing special token edge-cases.
